title: Tricyclic Antidepressants, SSRIs, and SNRIs: Mechanism and Clinical Applications

steps.title: TCA Pharmacological Profile
steps.tx: **Tricyclic antidepressant pharmacology** involves inhibition of presynaptic reuptake transporters for serotonin and norepinephrine, elevating monoamine neurotransmitter concentrations within synaptic clefts. However, tertiary amines like amitriptyline, imipramine, and clomipramine also exert potent antagonistic blockade at muscarinic acetylcholine receptors, histamine H1 receptors, and vascular alpha-1 adrenergic receptors, creating broad side-effect profiles.

steps.title: Specific Indications for TCAs
steps.tx: **Clinical indications for tricyclic agents** extend far beyond major depressive disorder due to unique receptor affinities. Clomipramine is the most serotonergic tricyclic and remains a formidable second-line medication for severe refractory obsessive-compulsive disorder. Imipramine remains historically celebrated for nocturnal enuresis, while low-dose amitriptyline provides effective prophylaxis for chronic tension headache and neuropathic pain.

steps.title: TCA Toxicity and Overdose
steps.tx: **Cardiotoxicity in TCA overdose** represents the foremost cause of fatality following self-poisoning, driven by blockade of cardiac fast voltage-gated sodium channels and delayed rectifier potassium channels. Electrocardiographic widening of the QRS complex beyond 100 milliseconds indicates substantial seizure risk, while a QRS duration exceeding 160 milliseconds reliably predicts life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias.

steps.tx: The width of the QRS, not the story of how many tablets were taken, forecasts the danger. **Cardiotoxicity in TCA overdose** is the main cause of death after self poisoning, from blockade of cardiac fast voltage gated sodium channels and of delayed rectifier potassium channels. Widening of the QRS beyond 100 milliseconds indicates a substantial risk of seizures. A QRS longer than 160 milliseconds reliably predicts life threatening ventricular arrhythmias. The prominent R wave in aVR is read together with that duration.
steps.say: Fatal tricyclic overdose is usually cardiac, because fast sodium channels and delayed rectifier potassium channels are blocked. A QRS beyond 100 milliseconds signals substantial seizure risk. A QRS beyond 160 milliseconds predicts life threatening ventricular arrhythmias. The tall R wave in aVR is interpreted with that QRS width.

steps.title: Antidote for TCA Toxicity
steps.tx: **Sodium bicarbonate therapy for TCA toxicity** serves as the definitive lifesaving intervention when the QRS complex exceeds 100 milliseconds or refractory hypotension develops. Hypertonic sodium bicarbonate provides an overwhelming extracellular sodium load that displaces tricyclic molecules from myocardial sodium channels, while alkalinizing serum to pH 7.45 to 7.55 to maximize non-ionized drug binding.

steps.title: SSRI Comparative Pharmacokinetics
steps.tx: **Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors differentiation** highlights distinctive pharmacokinetic traits: fluoxetine possesses the longest terminal elimination half-life of one to two weeks through its active metabolite norfluoxetine, minimizing abrupt withdrawal distress. Sertraline is preferred in coronary artery disease, paroxetine carries heavy anticholinergic sedation and teratogenic cardiac risks, and escitalopram exhibits the purest serotonergic selectivity.

steps.title: SNRIs and Noradrenergic Effects
steps.tx: **Dual action SNRIs** venlafaxine and duloxetine simultaneously inhibit both serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake transporters without blocking histamine, muscarinic, or adrenergic receptors. At dosages exceeding 150 milligrams daily, venlafaxine activates noradrenergic tone, producing sustained dose-dependent elevations in diastolic blood pressure. Duloxetine uniquely carries approved indications for diabetic peripheral neuropathy, chronic musculoskeletal pain, and fibromyalgia.

steps.title: Adverse Effects of SSRIs
steps.tx: **Common adverse effects of SSRIs** arise from stimulation of 5-HT2 and 5-HT3 receptors throughout the central nervous system and gastrointestinal tract, causing early nausea, loose stools, and sleep disturbance. Persistent sexual dysfunction occurs in up to 50 percent of long-term users, manifesting as delayed ejaculation, erectile difficulty, or anorgasmia, which often necessitates adjunctive bupropion or dose adjustment.

steps.title: Discontinuation Syndrome
steps.tx: **Antidepressant discontinuation syndrome symptoms** are remembered by the FINISH mnemonic: Flu-like malaise, Insomnia, Nausea, Imbalance, Sensory paresthesias described as electric brain zaps, and Hyperarousal. Symptoms erupt within two to four days of abrupt cessation, being particularly severe with short-acting paroxetine and venlafaxine, requiring gradual dose tapering over several weeks.
